pill.desc: very dark yellow to brownish orange, film-coated, ovaloid, scored tablet

clues.title: Approval
clues.text: First approved in May 2001 as a capsule. The film-coated tablet application followed in April 2003.

clues.title: Strengths
clues.text: Scored film-coated tablets in 100 and 400 mg. Held by Novartis, which also held the capsule application.

clues.title: Class
clues.text: A small-molecule protein-tyrosine kinase inhibitor, also active against the receptor kinases for PDGF and SCF (c-Kit).

clues.title: Target
clues.text: Blocks BCR-ABL, the constitutive kinase created by the Philadelphia chromosome abnormality, and induces apoptosis in cells that depend on it.

clues.title: Drug substance
clues.text: A mesylate salt of C₂₉H₃₁N₇O, MW 589.7. Soluble in aqueous buffers at pH 5.5 or below, very slightly soluble to insoluble at neutral and alkaline pH.

clues.title: Tablet
clues.text: Very dark yellow to brownish-orange film-coated tablets, coloured with red and yellow iron oxides. The 400 mg tablet is ovaloid, the 100 mg round.

clues.title: Absorption and binding
clues.text: Absolute oral bioavailability is 98%, with peak levels 2 to 4 hours after dosing. About 95% is bound to albumin and α₁-acid glycoprotein.

clues.title: Elimination
clues.text: Metabolized mainly by CYP3A4 to an N-demethylated piperazine metabolite of similar potency. Half-lives are about 18 and 40 hours; 68% of a dose appears in feces.

clues.title: Warnings
clues.text: No contraindications. Warnings include fluid retention and edema, hematologic toxicity, heart failure, hepatotoxicity and hemorrhage.

clues.title: Indications
clues.text: Indicated for Ph+ CML and Ph+ ALL, aggressive systemic mastocytosis, HES/CEL, DFSP, and Kit (CD117) positive GIST, among others.
